result.question: How has Nvidia's data center business contributed to its revenue growth across its last three fiscal years?
result.answer:
Nvidia's data center business has been the dominant engine of its revenue growth over the last three fiscal years, expanding from $47.5 billion in FY2024 to $115.2 billion in FY2025 and $193.7 billion in FY2026 [0001045810-26-000021:item-15-p037]. Over this period, total company revenue grew from $60.9 billion to $130.5 billion to $215.9 billion [0001045810-26-000021:item-15-p037]. Data Center revenue represented the majority of total revenue in each of these fiscal years, with Data Center revenue of $47,525 million against total revenue of $60,922 million in FY2024, $115,186 million against $130,497 million in FY2025, and $193,737 million against $215,938 million in FY2026 [0001045810-26-000021:item-15-p037].

**FY2024 (ended January 28, 2024):** Data Center revenue was $47.5 billion, up 217% from FY2023's $15.0 billion [0001045810-25-000023:item-15-p038]. This growth was driven by strong demand for the NVIDIA Hopper GPU computing platform used for training and inferencing of large language models, recommendation engines, and generative AI applications [0001045810-24-000124:part-i--item-2-p006]. Within Data Center, Compute revenue was $39.0 billion and Networking revenue was $8.6 billion [0001045810-26-000021:item-15-p037]. 

**FY2025 (ended January 26, 2025):** Data Center revenue reached $115.2 billion, a 142% increase from FY2024 [0001045810-26-000021:item-15-p037]. Revenue growth was driven by data center compute and networking platforms for accelerated computing and AI solutions, with demand for the Hopper architecture driving significant full-year growth [0001045810-25-000023:item-7-p001]. Nvidia began shipping production systems of the Blackwell architecture in the fourth quarter of FY2025 [0001045810-25-000023:item-7-p001]. Within Data Center, Compute revenue was $102.2 billion and Networking revenue was $13.0 billion [0001045810-26-000021:item-15-p037].

**FY2026 (ended January 25, 2026):** Data Center revenue reached $193.7 billion, a 68% increase from FY2025 [0001045810-26-000021:item-15-p037]. Revenue growth was again driven by data center compute and networking platforms for accelerated computing and AI solutions, with Blackwell architectures representing the majority of Data Center revenue [0001045810-26-000021:item-7-p001]. Within Data Center, Compute revenue was $162.4 billion and Networking revenue was $31.4 billion [0001045810-26-000021:item-15-p037].

In summary, the data center segment grew from $47.5 billion to $193.7 billion across the three fiscal years, representing the majority of total revenue in each year and contributing the largest share of Nvidia's revenue growth [0001045810-26-000021:item-15-p037]. The primary drivers were successive GPU architecture ramps — Hopper driving growth in FY2024 and FY2025 [0001045810-24-000029:item-7-p011] [0001045810-25-000023:item-7-p001], and Blackwell beginning shipments in Q4 FY2025 and representing the majority of Data Center revenue in FY2026 [0001045810-25-000023:item-7-p001] [0001045810-26-000021:item-7-p001] — fueled by global demand for AI training and inference infrastructure.
